skill.name: starknet-defi
skill.description: Build Starknet DeFi workflows for AVNU swaps, DCA orders, STRK staking, token data, and paymaster-backed transactions.
skill.summary: Use TypeScript examples to prepare and execute common Starknet DeFi operations.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: Most external-command detections are Markdown fence false positives, and most URL or environment detections are documentation or scoped configuration. The skill still requires signing authority and demonstrates irreversible DeFi execution without mandatory review, plus automatic slippage escalation.

remediation.issue: Raw private-key signing gives the agent direct control of account funds.
remediation.suggestion: Use a hardware, remote, or policy-limited signer. Never place a production private key in prompts, logs, or broadly accessible environment variables.

remediation.issue: Transaction examples submit irreversible actions without a mandatory approval step.
remediation.suggestion: Show the network, contract calls, amounts, fees, price impact, allowances, and recipient. Simulate first and require explicit approval before signing.

remediation.issue: The error handler automatically doubles slippage and retries.
remediation.suggestion: Set a strict maximum slippage, stop after any quote change, fetch a fresh quote, and require approval before retrying.

remediation.issue: The swap example executes the first returned quote without validating critical fields.
remediation.suggestion: Validate quote presence, token addresses, network, route, fees, price impact, expiry, and minimum received amount before building calls.

remediation.issue: The paymaster example falls back to a fixed external endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Allowlist supported hosts, require HTTPS, display the selected endpoint, and document what transaction metadata the service receives.

semantic_findings.title: Irreversible DeFi execution lacks an approval gate
semantic_findings.description: Live-account examples submit swaps, DCA orders, staking, and reward transactions without a required preview, simulation, spending cap, or explicit user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly call transaction execution functions with a signing account. No mandatory approval or simulation step appears before submission.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic slippage escalation has no safety cap
semantic_findings.description: On a slippage error, the helper doubles the caller-provided slippage and immediately retries. A large initial value can execute at unacceptable terms.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The retry branch directly multiplies slippage by two and resubmits. It has no maximum bound or user confirmation.

content.value_statement: Starknet DeFi actions require careful transaction construction and protocol-specific calls. This skill provides examples for swaps, DCA, staking, market data, and paymaster use.
actual_capabilities: Installs the documented Starknet and AVNU TypeScript dependencies.
Fetches AVNU quotes and builds or submits token swaps with configurable slippage.
Creates, lists, and cancels AVNU DCA orders.
Stakes STRK, checks positions, claims rewards, and performs unstaking steps.
Fetches verified token metadata, prices, and paginated token lists.
Configures AVNU paymaster support for gas payment in a selected token.
limitations: Requires a funded Starknet account, RPC access, and transaction-signing capability.
Lending and borrowing protocols are listed, but no implementation examples are included.
Examples lack mandatory simulation, transaction approval, allowance limits, and complete quote validation.
Package APIs, protocol contracts, endpoints, fees, and staking terms can change after publication.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Starknet swap
use_cases.description: Prepare a token quote, review routing and fees, then build a controlled AVNU swap flow.

use_cases.title: Automate recurring purchases
use_cases.description: Create, inspect, and cancel DCA orders while keeping amounts, frequency, and approvals explicit.

use_cases.title: Evaluate staking and token data
use_cases.description: Retrieve token prices and staking information before planning a carefully reviewed STRK transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a DeFi flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this skill handles a Starknet token swap. Describe prerequisites, quote fields, fees, approvals, and risks without submitting a transaction.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a swap plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an AVNU swap plan for [amount] [sell token] to [buy token] on [network]. Show validation and approval steps before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design a DCA workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DCA workflow for [total amount], [order count], and [frequency]. Include balance checks, cancellation handling, simulation, and explicit approval.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an execution workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Starknet DeFi workflow for signer exposure, quote validation, slippage bounds, allowance scope, contract addresses, paymaster trust, and transaction confirmation.

output_examples.input: Prepare a plan to swap 0.1 ETH for STRK without executing it.
output: Network and account prerequisites to verify.
Quote details including expected output, fees, price impact, route, and expiry.
A bounded slippage recommendation and minimum received amount.
A final transaction preview requiring explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Plan ten daily STRK purchases using 100 USDC and explain cancellation.
output: A DCA schedule with ten 10 USDC orders.
Checks for token decimals, balance, allowance, network, and start time.
A review step before creation and instructions for listing or cancelling open orders.

output_examples.input: Review the sample slippage retry behavior.
output_examples.output: The automatic retry is unsafe because it doubles slippage without a cap or renewed approval. Fetch a fresh quote and require confirmation.

best_practices: Start on Sepolia or with a low-value account, then verify network, token addresses, amounts, decimals, and recipients.
Use an isolated signer with limited funds. Never expose private keys in prompts, source files, logs, or shared environments.
Simulate every transaction, cap slippage and allowances, review fees and price impact, then require explicit approval before signing.
anti_patterns: Do not submit a transaction because the first quote exists or appears cheapest.
Do not increase slippage automatically after failure or retry with changed terms without approval.
Do not give an autonomous agent unrestricted access to a production private key or high-value account.

faq.question: Does this skill execute real Starknet transactions?
faq.answer: The examples can submit real transactions when connected to a funded account and signer. Review and approve every transaction before execution.

faq.question: Which DeFi operations have implementation examples?
faq.answer: The document includes swaps, DCA creation and cancellation, STRK staking actions, token prices, token discovery, and paymaster-backed swaps.

faq.question: Does it implement lending or borrowing?
faq.answer: No. It names zkLend and Nostra as references, but it does not provide lending or borrowing implementation examples.

faq.question: Can it perform gasless swaps?
faq.answer: It shows AVNU paymaster configuration for paying transaction fees with a supported token. Availability and terms depend on the selected network and service.

faq.question: How should signing keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use an isolated hardware, remote, or policy-limited signer. Never paste a private key into a prompt or store it in source code.

faq.question: What should be checked before a swap?
faq.answer: Verify the network, token addresses, decimals, amount, balance, allowance, route, price impact, fees, expiry, slippage, and minimum received amount.
